thread.title_full: Trump administration threatens to withhold SNAP funding from Michigan

author: Gia Verma
title: Trump administration threatens to withhold SNAP funding from Michigan
text:
On Tuesday, President Donald Trump’s administration threatened to begin withholding funds for administering the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program in most Democrat-controlled states, including Michigan, starting next week if these states do not provide personal data on individual SNAP recipients.
SNAP assisted about 41.7 million people per month in 2024, with the benefits fully funded by the federal government. However, during the government shutdown, federal funding for the program ran out, causing nearly 42 million Americans, including 1.47 million in Michigan, to experience delays in receiving food stamp benefits.
In May, the U.S. Department of Agriculture, which splits the cost of administering SNAP benefits with states, ordered the states to provide detailed personal data on each SNAP recipient including but not limited to their name, Social Security number and in one case, citizenship status, to maintain their federal funding.
More than 20 states, including Michigan, have filed a lawsuit over the requests. The lawsuit states the demands violate the Privacy Act of 1974 and the Paperwork Reduction Act. In a press release, Nessel said the order to provide personal information was an attempt by the Trump administration to misuse data from SNAP recipients for political purposes.
“This is yet another attempt by the Trump Administration to illegally use personal, sensitive data to fuel the president’s political agenda under the guise of fighting fraud and abuse,” Nessel said. “My colleagues and I will not allow this administration to trample on constitutional protections or unlawfully exploit the SNAP program in this way. Michigan families deserve to have their personal information protected, and I will keep fighting until they receive exactly that.”
Secretary of Agriculture Brooke Rollins said in a press release the new requirements were implemented to ensure only those who are eligible receive SNAP benefits.
“President Trump is rightfully requiring the federal government to have access to all programs it funds,” Rollins said. “SNAP is no exception. For years, this program has been on autopilot, with no USDA insight into real-time data. The Department is focused on appropriate and lawful participation in SNAP, and today’s request is one of many steps to ensure SNAP is preserved for only those eligible.”
28 states have since complied with the administration’s requests.
In an X post on Tuesday, Rollins wrote states must abide by these new regulations and accused them of trying to misuse federal funds.
“If a state won’t share data on criminal use of SNAP benefits, it won’t get a dollar of federal SNAP administrative funding,” Rollins wrote. “Let’s see which states stand for accountability and which are just protecting their bribery schemes.”
Daily Staff Reporter Gia Verma can be reached at giaverma@umich.edu.
